Scarlet's voice (`public/audio/f_attack`, `f_pain`, `f_death`) was trimmed and level-matched from
two more CC0 packs on OpenGameArt.org:

| Pack | Author | License | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Female RPG Voice Starter Pack (voice "Type 3": attack, jump, damaged) | Cici Fyre | CC0 | https://opengameart.org/content/female-rpg-voice-starter-pack |
| Female Hurt Grunts & Groans | AuraVoice | CC0 | https://opengameart.org/content/female-hurt-grunts-groans |

The rooftop's rain is the *AMB Rain Loop 1* above (layered twice, offset). Its thunder, distant
sirens, splashing footsteps and city rumble are synthesized at runtime (Web Audio noise and
oscillators), like the rest of the procedural score.

## Motion capture

The fighters' locomotion (stance idle, walk, jog, run, sprint, backward walk and side
shuffle) is retargeted from the **CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database**,
[mocap.cs.cmu.edu](http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu) — trials 13_17, 35_01, 35_17, 16_46, 09_06,
141_31 and 141_33; the clinch knee from trial 86_06, and the get-ups from trials 140_08 (off the
back) and 140_01 (face down), calibrated on 140_06. The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The
database was created with funding from NSF EIA-0196217. The CMU terms allow the data to be
included in products; it may not be resold on its own. `tools/mocap/convert.py` turns the
original ASF/AMC files into the normalised tracks in `src/anim/mocap/cmu.json`.

The fighters' strikes, kicks and evasions are retargeted from the **Open Motion Project** by
the Advanced Computing Center for the Arts and Design (**ACCAD**), The Ohio State University —
[accad.osu.edu/research/motion-lab](https://accad.osu.edu/research/motion-lab/mocap-system-and-data),
licensed under [CC BY 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Takes used, all from
the *Male2* martial-arts set: A1_Stand (calibration), E1_JabLeft, E4_CrossRight, E5_HookLeft,
E6_HookRight, E7_UppercutLeft, E10_BodyHookRight, E11_BackfistLeft, E14_BodyCrossRight,
E16_BodyJabLeft, G1_SidekickLeadingLeft, G2_FrontKick, G4_SpinningBackKick, G6_AxeKick,
G9_RoundhouseRight, G10_RoundhouseLeadingLeft, G13_CrescentRight, G15_RoundhouseBodyRight,
G17_PushKickLeft, G19_ReverseSpinCrescentLeft, E6_QuickRetreat and C24_QuickSidestepLeft. The
motion was cut, retimed, retargeted to the game's skeleton and cleaned up (contacts, floor,
foot rotations) by `tools/mocap/strikes.py` into `src/anim/mocap/strikes.json`; the elbow strike
folds the arm of the rear-hook take, and the side-step's arms are blended towards a guard.

## Scarlet's model

Scarlet is **Female_Adult_07** from the **Microsoft Rocketbox Avatar Library**
([github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Rocketbox](https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Rocketbox)),
released under the MIT license (notice below). `tools/models/rocketbox.mjs` converted the avatar's
FBX (its fingers curled into fists, its 81 bones mapped onto the game's 22) into
`src/character/models/scarlet/mesh.json`; `tools/models/scarlet_textures.py` re-dressed its
textures as Scarlet's (a black leather jacket over a red top, sheer black tights, black boots,
fingerless gloves, red hair and lips) into the images beside it. The leather mini skirt is built by
the game over the fitted body (`src/character/realBody.ts`).

## Art and animation

All other character meshes and textures, the environment art and the music are generated
procedurally by the game's own code. The punches, kicks, knee, evasions and get-ups
are the motion capture above; hit reactions, paired counters, finishers and takedowns, the flying
knee, the moves against someone behind and weapon attacks are authored in code (no free capture
of them was found: the open databases have no hit reactions or two-person fights, and their
weapon takes are mimed).
